sections.h2: How can you sell a Lewisville house fast?
sections.html:
Lewisville owners can sell fast to a cash buyer or through a listing, and which one fits depends on repairs and how soon you need the money. The city sits in Denton County in the north Dallas-Fort Worth area, and its rules on rentals and taxes shape what investors and owner-occupants will pay.

If the house has been a rental, check the city's rental inspection and short-term rental rules first, since buyers who plan to keep it as a rental will ask.

sections.h2: What does Lewisville say about its own taxes?
sections.html:
The city's budget page says Lewisville adopted a fiscal 2026 rate of $0.419009 per $100, its lowest since 1987, and that the rate has risen three times and fallen nine times in 28 years. Because the page also prints a comparison rate of .422435 for another year, ask the Denton County tax office for the rate on your own bill.

For a median residential bill of $6,606, the city reports that 65 percent goes to Lewisville ISD, 24 percent to the city and 11 percent to Denton County. A penny on the city rate raises about $2.154 million. Those shares tell a seller that the school district drives most of what a buyer will pay each year.

sections.h2: Do Lewisville rental rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. Lewisville runs an inspection program for single-family rentals, with no fee or registration, that began July 1, 2008. An inspection is triggered when the owner or future tenant notifies the city, when a tenant requests a water transfer, or on a complaint.

Minor violations do not block move-in, but life-safety issues do. The inspection covers items like a posted address, maintained roofing, gutters and siding, working windows, fences, an accessible water meter, trimmed vegetation near the right-of-way, and no inoperable vehicles or stagnant water. The program does not cover apartments, mobile homes or houses outside city limits. Fixing these items before listing can remove a common buyer objection.

sections.h2: How does Lewisville handle code enforcement on a house you plan to sell?
sections.html:
Lewisville's Code Enforcement Division handles complaints and the rental inspection program, and the city's rental inspection page gives 972.219.3470 as the contact number. Property standards on the inspection list give a good checklist for any seller, rented or not.

  • House number visible from the street.
  • Roof, gutters, siding and exterior doors in repair.
  • Windows and screens intact, and fences or pool fences maintained.
  • Electrical service drop at least 10 feet above the ground and the meter secured.
  • Grass, weeds, hedges and trees along the right-of-way trimmed.
  • No inoperable vehicles, no cars parked on grass and no standing water.

An owner who clears these items before listing avoids a code complaint that can surface during a sale. If the house is leased, the city says an inspection happens when the owner or future tenant tells the city, when a tenant requests water service, or after a complaint. Minor findings do not stop a tenant from moving in.

sections.h2: What are the short-term rental limits in Lewisville?
sections.html:
Lewisville issues short-term rental permits yearly and stops at 150 active ones. The city's page prints these terms.

Lewisville short-term rental rules as printed on the City of Lewisville page
ItemRule
Permit termOne year, not transferable
Application fee$400, non-refundable
Active permit cap150
Spacing, single-family or duplex1,000 feet between rentals
Multifamily limit3% of units or 2 units, whichever is greater

Permits stay with the owner and address, so a buyer who wants to host guests must apply fresh with no promise of approval. The city says existing permitted rentals are treated as legal non-conforming until use stops for six months. Hotel occupancy tax is reported monthly.

sections.h2: How do Denton County taxes work for a Lewisville seller?
sections.html:
Bills arrive in the fall and are usually due by January 31. The lien attaches on January 1, so the owner on that date is responsible for the year's tax.

  • An over-65 or disabled homeowner can ask the county about a four-payment plan.
  • A value protest is due by May 15 or 30 days after notice, whichever comes later.
  • After the appraisal board, appeals can go to district court or arbitration.

Get a current payoff and tax statement from the Denton County tax office before closing.

sections.h2: What Texas rules apply if a Lewisville house is in trouble?
sections.html:
A lien for unpaid tax can end in a tax sale, and the Comptroller's pages describe redemption: land sold at a tax sale can be reclaimed within two years if it is a homestead, or 180 days otherwise, at a stated premium. Any excess from a tax foreclosure can be claimed by the former owner for two years.

If a tenant stays after a sale, the new owner may need a justice court eviction case, and the tenant gets at least four days' notice of the trial. Selling before any of this starts keeps your options open.

sections.h2: What should you have ready before accepting a Lewisville offer?
sections.html:
• A copy of the deed and any survey.
  • The latest Denton County tax statement and exemption list.
  • Rental inspection or short-term rental permit records, if the house was rented.
  • A payoff letter from your lender.

sections.h2: What do Lewisville's short-term rental details mean for a buyer?
sections.html:
The city's page adds details that matter if your house has been listed on a booking site. As of October 15, 2025, the city reported 116 active permits against the cap of 150, and the application closes when permits plus pending applications hit 150. It reopens if permits are denied, revoked or expire. Current holders can reapply at least 30 days before expiry even when applications are closed.

  • Bedrooms must be at least 70 square feet, and a bedroom shared by more than one person needs 50 square feet per occupant.
  • A 70 to 99 square foot bedroom counts as one occupant, and 100 to 149 as two.
  • Ads must show the permit number and say the unit cannot host paid events or parties.
  • More than two city code citations in a permit year can lead to revocation.

Because a permit cannot be transferred, the buyer starts from the application queue. Ask the city's permitting office at permitting@cityoflewisville.com or 972.219.3470 about current availability.

sections.h2: How should a Lewisville seller read the city's tax comparison?
sections.html:
The city compares itself with nine other North Texas cities using a $450,635 home. Its table lists Lewisville's total annual charges at $3,243, which is the lowest among the ten, and ranks the city first for value. The comparison includes property tax, water, sewer and rates at each city, and it is the city's own presentation rather than a market study.

Why mention it to a buyer? Low municipal charges are one of the few Lewisville advantages that survive any market, and the city says it ranked first in this survey for at least nine years. The same page splits the typical bill: $1,585 to the city, $727 to Denton County and $4,294 to Lewisville ISD for a median bill of $6,606.

City services listed on the page include public safety, parks, library services, engineering and neighborhood and inspections services.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lewisville house if it was a rental?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers may ask whether it passed the city's single-family rental inspection, so have any records ready.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over my Lewisville short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. The city says permits are not transferable, so a new owner must apply, and the 150 permit cap and spacing rules apply.

faqs.q: What is the Lewisville property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's budget page prints $0.419009 per $100 for fiscal 2026. Your full bill also includes Denton County and the school district, so check your statement.

faqs.q: When are Denton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: In most cases by January 31, with penalty and interest from February 1. Some owners can use a split or installment plan.

faqs.q: Do I need Lewisville city approval to sell my home?
faqs.a: No city approval is needed just to sell. Contact the city if you have open code violations or permits, since a buyer will want those resolved.
